scores.claim_text: As of June 30, 2024, Pony had registered 284 patents in China and 185 patents globally (incl. United States), reflecting a substantial autonomous-driving IP portfolio.
scores.M_value: Precise 'Pony.ai' search: 32 US applications, 15 granted pre-cutoff, 27/32 categorized 'autonomous' (autonomous-vehicle suspension control, sensor calibration/cleaning, evacuation systems, segmented sensor enclosures, timestamp synchronization). Broad 'Pony AI Inc.' assignee adds many more granted AV patents (HD city mapping, sensor fusion, vehicle health monitoring, sensor alignment, intent inference). Bare 'Pony' (264 apps) is substring-contaminated (Shenzhen Pony Systems rental apparatus) so the precise count governs.
scores.interpretation: USPTO independently corroborates a real, technically-coherent US patent portfolio squarely in the claimed autonomous-driving area (15+ granted US patents, all AV-domain). This is the inverse of the Nikola pattern (large IP claim, ~0 in claimed area). The 185-global / 284-China totals can't be exhaustively reconciled US-side, but the US registry confirms genuine AV IP depth -> claim corroborated.

scores.claim_text: Pony tested driverless vehicles in the United States (California): it held a California DMV driverless testing permit and filed a recall notice at NHTSA's request after an accident; it conducts independent R&D and testing in the US.
scores.M_value: vPIC returns 0 manufacturers for 'Pony'; 'Pony.ai' returns 404 (not a registered vehicle manufacturer).
scores.interpretation: NHTSA vPIC registers US-sold vehicle OEMs, not AV-technology companies holding state testing permits. Pony is a Cayman/China foreign private issuer and an AV software/tech company, not a vehicle OEM, so absence in vPIC is expected and NOT a contradiction (CALIBRATION heuristics 1 + 2). Critically the claim is self-deprecating: the prospectus voluntarily discloses the California DMV SUSPENDED its driverless testing permit after an accident and that it filed an NHTSA recall on request -- a candid negative disclosure, not an inflated milestone. No US federal registry covers the foreign-ops / state-AV-testing footprint asserted -> honestly UNVERIFIABLE, not manufactured severity.

scores.claim_text: Pony formed a joint venture with Toyota (TMC) and GTMC to mass-produce/deploy fully driverless robotaxis; Toyota is a strategic investor, principal shareholder and related party.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext 'Pony.ai' (all forms; and annual-report forms) cutoff 2024-11-27
scores.M_value: 33 total EDGAR fulltext hits for 'Pony.ai', including NVIDIA 8-Ks and 10-K, Luminar (LAZR) 10-K/8-Ks, Mobileye (MBLY) 10-K, and Aurora Innovation (AUR) 10-Ks. Multiple independent US-listed AV-ecosystem counterparties name Pony.ai by name. Toyota itself (foreign 20-F filer) is not directly searched, but the JV is backed in Pony's own audited financials by a US$2.6M (by 9/30/2024) + US$52.1M (by 9/30/2025) hard cash investment commitment and disclosed TMC engineering-service fees / related-party balances.
scores.interpretation: Pony.ai is corroborated as a real, named participant in the AV supply/partner ecosystem by NVIDIA, Luminar, Mobileye and Aurora filings -- the opposite of an inflation-suspect (0-mention) profile. The Toyota/GTMC JV is supported by hard, dated investment-commitment dollars in the audited notes; Toyota's strategic-investor role is a related-party fact, not a buyer-side obligation requiring separate Toyota disclosure (heuristic 4). Partnership claim corroborated.

scores.claim_text: Pony operates a fleet of over 250 robotaxis that has accumulated over 33.5 million km of autonomous mileage (incl. 3.9M km driverless), with PonyPilot public fare-charging service in all four China Tier-1 cities.
scores.interpretation: Robotaxi fleet size, cumulative-km and the PonyPilot consumer app are China-market operational metrics. No US federal registry (NHTSA covers US-sold vehicles only; EPA/USAspending/openFDA do not apply) and no US counterparty discloses a China robotaxi app. Absence is expected for a foreign private issuer's domestic operations (CALIBRATION heuristics 1, 2) -> UNVERIFIABLE, not underdelivery. Internally consistent with the disclosed Safety Production Fund (1% of freight revenues) and operating-vehicle capex.

scores.claim_text: Pony operates a fleet of over 190 robotrucks (incl. with Sinotrans, China's largest freight logistics company) accumulating ~5.0M km and 767M freight ton-kilometers.
scores.M_value: 40 EDGAR hits for 'Sinotrans' but none are Pony-relevant -- they are Americold, EHang, Dynagas LNG, Sino-Global Shipping etc. referencing the Sinotrans name in unrelated logistics/shipping contexts. No US filer discloses a Sinotrans-Pony robotruck arrangement.
scores.interpretation: Robotruck fleet and the Sinotrans collaboration are China freight-logistics operations. Sinotrans is a China SOE not a US registrant; US-side counterparty disclosure is not expected (heuristics 2, 5). Internally, the related-party notes DO corroborate a real Sinotrans commercial relationship -- US$12.3M Virtual Driver operation-service fees from Sinotrans in 1H2024 and finance/operating leases -- consistent with the claimed collaboration. No US registry covers the operational metrics -> UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: Pony partnered with leading China OEMs SAIC, GAC and FAW to co-develop and mass-produce robotaxi vehicles, and with SANY to co-develop Level 4 robotrucks.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext 'Pony.ai' forms=20-F,40-F,10-K cutoff 2024-11-27 (proxy for ecosystem-counterparty disclosure)
scores.M_value: 12 annual-report hits naming 'Pony.ai' (NVIDIA, Luminar, Mobileye, Aurora) confirm Pony as a recognized AV player, but the specific OEM partners SAIC, GAC, FAW, SANY, GTMC are Chinese manufacturers that do not file with the SEC and appear in no US registry.
scores.interpretation: Pony's overall legitimacy as a real AV company is independently corroborated (peer-/supplier-side mentions in NVIDIA/Luminar/Mobileye/Aurora annual reports). But each named China OEM co-development partnership is a foreign-counterparty operational claim with no US registry coverage and no US-listed counterparty to disclose it (heuristics 2, 5). No basis to confirm or contradict the specific SAIC/GAC/FAW/SANY co-development arrangements -> UNVERIFIABLE.
